clue.text: Have a fit, finally, as part of blazing row in town

indicators.note: as part of says the letters are taken from inside the run of words blazing row in town

explanation.surface: A furious argument erupts somewhere in a town and someone finally loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a fit' suggests a tantrum, but the sense is clothes that come to fit; the letters run across blazinG ROW IN TOwn.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a child eventually fills out oversized clothes, so they come to fit at last.

clue.text: Over and over again, interrupting journey north for detective

indicators.note: interrupting means the two letters break into the reversed word at separate points
again says the breaking-in is done a second time, with the repeated over making its own cut into the reversed word
in a down clue, going north means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a journey is a trip
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a second cricket over gives another O

explanation.surface: Something keeps repeating during a trip northwards, and a detective is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: PIRT, the upward reading of TRIP, takes one O after P and the other after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's famous Belgian private investigator.

clue.text: Look for some 12 who deal with cuts

definitions.meaning: a ... (from ... hook) is a look, as in have a ...
12 is the tradesfolk entry; meat traders who sell cuts are one kind

explanation.walkthrough: BUTCHER'S HOOK is Cockney rhyming slang for look, shortened to butcher's.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang gives a glance; separately, meat retailers are a kind of tradespeople handling joints.

clue.text: Good sort including East European in drive

indicators.note: including means the first word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: Chambers lists toff as a good sort, a decent chap

explanation.surface: A decent chap takes an Eastern European along on a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' is the golfing sense: the opening shot from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to start a hole by striking the ball from its peg is the opening drive.

clue.text: French star having party in pub before closing time

indicators.note: in means the party word sits inside the pub plus closing letter

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: closing picks out the final letter of the word time

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A French celebrity holds a party in a pub just before last orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing time' looks like last orders, but closing takes only the final letter of time; DO goes inside BART.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigitte Bardot is a French film actress, a star of 1950s and 1960s cinema.

clue.text: Worker, perhaps, holding up excessively small footwear

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the next piece

parts.note: a worker is a kind of bee, so bee is an example

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: excessively means too, as in too much

explanation.surface: A worker is holding up some ridiculously tiny shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' in a down clue reads the word for excessively upwards; 'perhaps' flags the worker as just one example of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootee is a soft knitted shoe for a baby, hence small.

clue.text: Learners that you finally supplied with driving aids

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each of the words that and you

parts.note: golf tees hold the ball for a drive

explanation.surface: Students are given aids for learning to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving aids' looks like a car, but golf tees support the ball for a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Students taught by a tutor are pupils, people learning.

clue.text: Mishandled pistol went off

definitions.note: verb past tense, as food goes bad

indicators.note: something mishandled is knocked about, so the letters of pistol are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gun was handled badly and went off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went off' sounds like the pistol firing, but it is the definition: food that went off spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone bad has rotted, perished or turned.

clue.text: Tools gripping inside of ear for piercing operations

indicators.note: gripping means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: tools are implements

indicators.note: inside of picks out the central letter of the word ear

explanation.surface: Tools grip the inner ear during an ear-piercing procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside of ear' looks anatomical, but takes only the middle letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaling is running something through with a spike, so these are acts of piercing.

clue.text: Coward's end is elsewhere in conflict at sea

indicators.note: end is elsewhere means the final letter of the word coward is moved to another place

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A coward's demise takes place far from a naval battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the end of COWARD moves to the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cod Wars were fishing-rights disputes between Britain and Iceland fought by naval vessels.

clue.text: Minimal intelligence?

parts.note: suggests a dim mind, but means spy information shrunk to a tiny photographic dot

explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' is espionage material, not brainpower; 'Minimal' means physically tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Spies reduced documents to a tiny photograph the size of a full stop, hiding secret information.

clue.text: Youngster's finishes counting towards score

definitions.meaning: an adolescent aged thirteen to nineteen
the endings of thirteen to nineteen, the numbers counting up to twenty, a score

explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty; the numbers just short of it all end the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for an adolescent, and the ending that the numbers thirteen to nineteen share.

clue.text: Folder with task organised for dealers

indicators.note: organised means the letters of folder and task are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out a folder of tasks for some traders.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopkeepers and merchants are people who trade, so they are dealers.

clue.text: Complete parts of it repeatedly, as in some places here

definitions.text: Complete parts of it repeatedly, as in some places here

parts.words: Complete parts of it repeatedly, as in some places here
parts.note: parts of it are the letters i and t; finishing each of them over and over, as the grid does with its DOT and TEE answers

annotation.spelling: DOT THE I'S AND CROSS THE T'S

explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'it' are completed with a dot and a cross; the grid holds many answers containing DOT and TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for attending to every last small detail, finishing a task thoroughly.

clue.text: Bound to find them, oddly, on the left

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of the word them

parts.note: only some letters of them are used
taken as written
red means left-wing in politics

explanation.surface: You are certain to find them on the left, if oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like certain to, but Bound is the definition; THE is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied up or fastened by a rope, so restrained.

clue.text: Able to figure out true mean, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means the letters of true and mean are put together in some other order

explanation.surface: Someone capable of working out what the true average is, somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure out' reads as a phrase, but 'figure' means calculate and 'out' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being competent with numbers and arithmetic is the counterpart of literate.

clue.text: Skill is found around old part of France

indicators.note: found around means the words skill and is enclose the next piece

parts.note: skill is art

explanation.surface: Skill is found in an old region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Artois is a historic province in northern France, now within Pas-de-Calais.

clue.text: Tree in which rook sits before moving

definitions.meaning: to tree is to trap a hunted animal, chase it up a tree

definitions.text: in which rook sits before moving
definitions.meaning: on a chessboard the rook starts in the end square of the board

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree' is a verb, to trap; the rook is the chess piece, not a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapping a quarry with no way out, and the edge square where each chess rook begins.

clue.text: See 13
First section's set up for governor once

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: the first section of a document is Part A, and the possessive gives S

explanation.surface: The opening section has been arranged by a historical governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial ruler in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: Piece of furniture in which to put a kind of shirt

parts.note: to put is to set, as in set it down
a tee is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture in which to keep a certain shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a long upholstered seat for several people.

clue.text: Unsettled, with low temperature

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

explanation.surface: Unsettled weather, with a low temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' reads as an adjective with temperature, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is open to debate, so not yet decided.

clue.text: Sit exam — holding it back is extremely silly

indicators.note: holding means the first phrase contains the next piece

parts.note: to sit an exam is to do a test

indicators.note: back means the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Sitting an exam while holding it back is the silliest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the clue's own word it around before it goes into the phrase for sitting an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of dotty, meaning crazy or eccentric, so most foolish.

clue.text: A lot of people in the wrong — setter and solver backed out

indicators.note: out means the letters are taken away from the words the wrong
backed means the pair of letters is read backwards

parts.note: the setter and the solver together are we

explanation.surface: A crowd turns on someone in the wrong; the setter and solver withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns WE into EW, which comes out of THE WRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large crowd, a mass of people.

clue.text: In this way, editor is influenced

indicators.note: In says the letters lie inside the run of words this way, editor

explanation.surface: An editor has been swayed in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across thiS WAY EDitor.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway someone is to persuade them, so swayed means persuaded.

clue.text: Uncertainly move infant in discomfort? Not hot, however

indicators.note: Not means the letter for hot is left out

parts.note: a teether is a baby cutting its teeth, painful
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A distressed baby shifts uncertainly, though not because it is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to wobble or sway unsteadily.
